sources.title: BOE notice: public information on the SET Enlace 400/220 kV substation and 400 kV supply line SE Riocaya - SET Enlace for the connection of the Data Center Nostrum Evergreen, Badajoz
sources.publisher: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado
sources.attribution: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado
sources.summary: BOE no. 228 of 15 September 2026 (section V-B): the Industry and Energy Area of the Government Delegation in Extremadura opens 30 working days of public information on the application by Data Riocaya, SLU (filed 18 August 2025) for prior and construction authorisation of the SET Enlace 400/220 kV substation and a 291.96 m single-circuit 400 kV overhead line from Red Eléctrica's Riocaya 400 kV substation, whose stated purpose is to connect "the future Data Center (DC) Nostrum Evergreen of 300 MW" to the transmission grid in the municipality of Badajoz. Red Eléctrica granted access and connection for the consumption installation Nostrum Evergreen (DC Badajoz) at Riocaya 400 kV on 31 May 2023. The notice states that the data centre itself, its SE DC Badajoz 220/20 kV substation and the four 220 kV underground lines between the two substations are processed in separate files, and that the 220 kV side is processed before the Junta de Extremadura. Execution budget EUR 12,726,868.47.
sources.date_semantics: Notice dated 11 September 2026, published 15 September 2026; the publication date is used as the announcement observation of the named future data centre. It concerns a pending grid-connection application: no authorisation of the data centre, permit, or physical work is established.
sources.official_reference: Anuncio del Área de Industria y Energía de la Delegación del Gobierno en Extremadura, 11/09/2026; BOE núm. 228, 15/09/2026, págs. 48527-48530; BOE-B-2026-29930

sources.publisher: Diario Oficial de Extremadura (Junta de Extremadura)
sources.attribution: Junta de Extremadura, Diario Oficial de Extremadura
sources.summary: DOE no. 173 of 7 September 2026: the regional Directorate-General for Industry, Energy and Mines grants Data Riocaya, SLU prior administrative authorisation (not construction authorisation) for the regional-competence electrical consumption infrastructure of the Data Center Nostrum Evergreen (DC Badajoz): the 220 kV yard of the 400/220 kV link substation, two 220 kV underground supply lines of 3,342.74 m and 3,276.91 m to the SE DC Badajoz 220/20 kV substation, and that substation (six 110/150 MVA transformers plus two future), sited "en plataforma logística, 06006", Badajoz. It recites that Decreto 151/2025 declared the data-centre project a Proyecto Empresarial de Interés Autonómico and that the environmental body will report on the global Data Center Nostrum Evergreen project.

sources.title: DOE: Decreto 151/2025, de 11 de noviembre, declaring the Data Riocaya, SLU sustainable data-computing and AI centre in Badajoz a Proyecto Empresarial de Interés Autonómico
sources.publisher: Diario Oficial de Extremadura (Junta de Extremadura)
sources.attribution: Junta de Extremadura, Diario Oficial de Extremadura
sources.summary: DOE no. 221 of 17 November 2025: the Junta de Extremadura declares the project presented by Data Riocaya, SLU (application of 29 May 2025) for a new-generation data centre in the Plataforma Logística del Suroeste Europeo, Badajoz, designed for grid access of up to 300 MW electrical, a Proyecto Empresarial de Interés Autonómico, with planned investment of EUR 1,913,163,000 and 330 annual work units of employment. The data centre is to be located on plots L.I-12, L.I-13, C.E.S-2, C.E.S-4 and C.E.S-4A of the platform, 222,735 m2 in total; associated works are an adjacent 220/30 kV substation, a 400/220 kV link substation and high-voltage lines. The qualification carries a declaration of public utility and urgent occupation for the 220 kV link-substation yard and underground supply line.
sources.date_semantics: Decree of 11 November 2025 published 17 November 2025; outside the admission window and used only for project identity and the plot list behind the locator. A regional-interest qualification is not development consent or a building permit.

sources.title: City of Prineville City Council meeting of 13 October 2026: agenda packet, including Resolution No. 1654 and the development agreement with Apple, Inc. for the PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project
sources.summary: Item 7 of the 13 October 2026 council agenda is Resolution 1654 authorizing a development agreement between the City and Apple, Inc. The draft resolution recites that Apple, Inc. owns and operates a data center within Prineville city limits that requires offsite utility infrastructure, and recital A of the attached agreement states that Apple owns and operates a data center campus on real property within the City (Exhibit A). The staff report explains that Apple's initial development plan included expansion of the eastern portion of its campus, which needs offsite utilities: a 16-inch domestic water main, 12-inch non-potable water main, 21-inch sanitary sewer, 12-inch reclaimed/industrial wastewater main, 8-inch gravity and 4-inch pressure sewer lines, bored under Highway 126 in the vicinity of SW High Desert Drive and SW Baldwin Road, serving the eastern portion of the campus, the PRZ 06 development area. The City procures and inspects the work, Apple reimburses up to USD 8,803,435.44 plus an 8.5 percent administrative fee, and the City is to strive for Final Completion by 31 March 2028 and reserve water capacity (99 gpm current plus 350 gpm future). Exhibit A, a Parametrix aerial plan, labels the APPLE CAMPUS north-east of Prineville Airport and east of the SW Connect Way buildings; its flow table assumes 4000 gpm to Apple plus peak demands to Meta and airport industrial users.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is the creation time of the AgendaCenter packet PDF (2026-10-08T17:29:07Z per its PDF metadata); the AgendaCenter index shows no posting timestamp. The operating statement is the City's present-tense recital in the resolution and agreement prepared for the 13 October meeting and is taken as observed on the packet date. The utility completion date and water capacities are forecasts and reservations, not observations. Named officials are public officials acting in office and are not restated; the agreement's invoicing e-mail address is not restated.
sources.personal_data_note: No names, phone numbers or e-mail addresses are copied from the packet.

sources.title: Laramie County Board of Commissioners memo to residents, 8 July 2026: Project Tembo Data Center Site Plan and Conditional Use Permit
sources.publisher: Laramie County, Wyoming (Board of County Commissioners)
sources.summary: The Board of County Commissioners informs residents about a Commercial Site Plan re-submittal and a Conditional Use Permit for a data-center development previously known as Project Jade, now Project Tembo. The earlier submittal, applied for by Crusoe Energy, received governing-body approvals for a zone change to the Switchgrass Industrial Park Planned Unit Development and for the Commercial Site Plan, after public hearings; Tallgrass Energy received matching zone-change and site-plan approvals for the natural-gas Power Hub, whose construction phases are described as well underway. Crusoe has since withdrawn, and the county has discussed the re-submittal with Google (d.b.a. Jupiter Star Holdings, LLC). The revised application reduces the project from five to four buildings (4,025,500 to 3,080,000 sq ft), adds a second permanent entrance on US 85 and halves the peak construction workforce (5,000 to 2,500); because it is smaller than the previously approved Site Plan the county intends to process the Site Plan Revision administratively. A Class B CUP (PZ-26-00057) and commercial site plan for an Office Complex, part of the overall Project Tembo site-plan submittal PZ-26-00058, located directly east of the Switchgrass Industrial Park beside US 85, were to be heard by the Planning Commission on 13 August 2026.
sources.date_semantics: Dated memo (8 July 2026; PDF created the same day). It is the county's statement of the approvals already granted and of the pending revision; future hearings and construction are forecasts. Named commissioners are public officials acting in office and are not restated.
